crypto-lab-ablation-wire.note: Rust crypto core reviewed; WASM is built from that core

crypto-lab-adaptor-gate.note: secp256k1 is added by review because the scanner now reads `import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js'` as a module path rather than an implementation, which is right in general and wrong here: src/crypto/secp.ts wraps that import into the lab's own point and scalar layer (N, G, mulG, mul, liftX, invModN) and src/crypto/adaptor.ts computes the adaptor construction on it directly. The anchor is the defining point addition, R + T, not the import. Adaptor layer is the lab's own code over @noble/curves point/scalar ops; the completed signature is verified by the library's unmodified BIP-340 verify. Ledgers and PTLC routing are modeled and labelled as such in-page; PTLC settlement is causal (each hop consumes the value extracted downstream), not precomputed.

crypto-lab-biham-lens.note: Executes a toy SPN, not DES

crypto-lab-card-trick.note: Runs den Boer's physical-card AND protocol; no encryption

crypto-lab-collision-vault.note: The lab hashes with WebCrypto through one local helper, and names the algorithm only as that helper's STRING ARGUMENT: hashing/index.ts:79 is `return webcryptoDigest('SHA-256', bytes)` and :81 the SHA-512 case, while webcrypto.ts:25 does the work as `subtle().digest(algo, copy)` with algo a parameter. No line carries both the name and the operation, so no detection shape can reach it, and the only other place either name appears in executable code is a vectors table (SHA256_VECTORS, SHA512_VECTORS) - which is test data, not an implementation, and is now correctly suppressed. Reviewed by reading hashing/index.ts and hashing/webcrypto.ts in full: both digests are computed by the platform on the learner's input, which is the lab's whole subject. Anchored at the call sites rather than at the digest call, because those are the lines that say WHICH algorithm.

crypto-lab-export-grade.note: Runs TETRA TEA1 and a bounded state-recovery demonstration. Exhibits 5 and 6 add no cryptography: src/attack/rate.ts is arithmetic over the search Exhibit 3 already runs, and src/data/attacks.ts is a sourced citation table. AES-128/192/256 are named throughout that table and implemented nowhere in this lab.

crypto-lab-frost-threshold.note: Rust keygen, signing rounds and aggregation reviewed

crypto-lab-function-key.note: Browser TypeScript throughout, no other language and no WASM. Group operations are @noble/curves 2.4.0, pinned to RFC 9496 Appendix A (16 A.1 multiples both directions, 29 A.2 rejections, 8 A.3 map outputs) before any scheme code was written on it; ABDP15 Construction 3.1 and the baby-step giant-step, exact-rational and mod-l algebra are implemented in-repo. Five derived attacks are removed because none is an attack this lab shows, and each was matched by a different accident: Man-in-the-middle came from the string 'DH MITM' inside CATALOG-ENTRY.md, which is this catalog's own concept line quoted back in the lab's handoff doc and not lab source at all; Signature malleability from /malleab/i on a seed label, in a lab that has no signatures - what it demonstrates is CIPHERTEXT malleability, and its own source calls that 'not an attack and not a flaw in the proof'; Chosen-plaintext attack from CPA inside 'IND-FE-CPA', the security notion ABDP15 proves rather than an attack mounted; Chosen-ciphertext attack from CCA inside 'Any CCA security whatever', a line in the NOT-BUILT list; and Discrete log from 'baby step', which this lab pays as a decryption cost and never mounts. The two attacks it does show, key collusion and ciphertext malleability, have no term in the vocabulary. Baby-step giant-step is added by review: src/crypto/dlog.ts is a baby-step giant-step over a symmetric range, but it names the algorithm only in comments and in the local counters babySteps and giantSteps, and the exported function is called dlogSymmetric. The anchor is that function, not the counter a narrower shape used to read.

crypto-lab-pq-chooser.note: Derives every displayed public-key, ciphertext and signature size from real @noble/post-quantum output at page load rather than from constants; spec figures appear only as test oracles. Falcon ranges quoted in source are an offline 20,000-signature study, distinct from the live per-run range the table derives from FALCON_SAMPLES signatures. Classical baselines (X25519, ECDSA P-256, RSA-2048) are benchmarked by the same harness; RSA keygen is reported not-measured by design.

crypto-lab-sm9-forge.note: Implements the SM9 family in src/sm9/ — extraction for both master key pairs, signature, key exchange, KEM and public key encryption — over the BN256 curve and R-ate pairing, checked against the worked examples in the standard's annexes. SM3 and SM4 are imported, not implemented here. Boneh-Franklin IBE is drawn as the contrast to SM9's inversion, never computed. The comparison oracle is vendored GmSSL-JS, which is opaque to the scanner.

crypto-lab-vector-gate.note: Read src/crypto/ed25519.ts, src/main.ts and tools/check-oracles.py. The browser performs real Ed25519 verification with extended-coordinate BigInt arithmetic and WebCrypto SHA-512; both modes share decoder, challenge and equation, and differ only on S < L enforcement. The Ed25519 anchor is its verifier entry rather than the UI import. The Python file only cross-checks frozen fixtures with OpenSSL and libsodium; it is not hidden browser crypto. The derived side-channel attack is removed: src/main.ts mentions side-channel resistance only as evidence not established, and mounts no side-channel attack. Signature malleability is the actual one-predicate experiment. No ZIP215 comparison, ECDSA or ML-KEM computation is implemented here.
